newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government bonds lower on interbank rate.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government bonds lower on interbank rate.

text.p: Singapore government bonds ended lower in moderate trade on retail and interbank interest, dealers said on Monday.
"Bond prices were slightly higher following a small decline in the interbank rate. Treasury bill yields were slightly lower. Volume was moderate," a local dealer said.

Among bonds, July 1998 closed at S$99.32/99.37 compared with last Friday's close of S$99.30/99.35, September 2001 at S$97.37/97.42 against S$97.27/97.32 and June 2003 at S$95.37/95.42 from S$95.27/95.32.
The overnight interbank offered rate eased to 3-3/8 3-1/4 percent against last Friday's 3-9/16 3-7/16 percent.

In treasury bills, three-months ended at a yield of 0.60/0.55 percent from last Friday's yield of 0.88/0.83 percent and one-year at a yield of 1.28/1.23 percent versus last Friday's 1.38/1.33 percent.
